assets.conditionNote: Ways lubricated with Mobil Vactra No. 2; X/Y backlash within specification (0.002").

loto.authorizedPersonnel: Sr. Instructional Lab Supervisor (Max Wright) & Student Research Assistants (SRAs)
loto.normalShutdown: Turn power switch to middle OFF position (Top left front face).

energySources.isolationLocation: Switch box to the right of Mill on fence post.
energySources.isolationProcedure: Pull switch box lever down to OFF and install LOTO padlock (from machine shop cage or welding room) through lever.

loto.storedEnergyRelief: Allow spindle and drive pulley assembly to coast to a complete stop.
loto.zeroEnergyVerification: Press black power button and verify spindle does not power on when mill switch is toggled.

ppe: NO GLOVES While Spindle is Rotating
hazards: Rotating spindle, collet, and cutting tool entanglement hazard
Flying hot chips and broken cutter ejection
Pinch hazard between moving table and knee saddle
beforeUse: Check drawbar engagement and verify collet/tooling is properly seated.
Set speed via variable speed dial ONLY while spindle is running, or shift Hi-Neutral-Lo range lever ONLY when spindle is completely stopped.
duringUse: Verify quill lock and table locks are set appropriately for the cut.
Confirm climb vs. conventional milling setup (use conventional milling on manual leadscrews to prevent cutter grab).
Never reach around a rotating cutter or adjust workpiece while spindle is turning.
afterUse: Return machine to showroom condition (brush chips with shop brush—NEVER use compressed air).
Home and wipe down table, ways, and vise.
Remove collets/tooling from spindle and return to designated tool rack.
sop.emergencyProtocol: Turn rotary drum switch to center OFF position or disengage main disconnect lever on right fence post; notify Lab Supervisor or SRA immediately.

checklist: Fill one-shot lubricator (Mobil Vactra No. 2) & verify oil film on X/Y/Z ways
Check quill feed engagement & clock spring return tension
Measure & log X/Y leadscrew backlash (0.000")
Check X/Y/Z gib strip play and adjust if excessive
Inspect vari-speed belt/pulley wear & check backgear noise
Stone table T-slots to remove burrs or dings

loto.normalShutdown: Depress red OFF button (Front Control Panel), turn main power switch counterclockwise to OFF (Right Rear Control Panel).

energySources.isolationLocation: Circuit panel on North Wall (Breaker 1-3-5).
energySources.isolationProcedure: Switch Breaker 1-3-5 to OFF and apply Snap-On Circuit Breaker Lockout with LOTO padlock and tag.

loto.storedEnergyRelief: Ensure Z-axis head is resting in safe position and spindle is completely stopped.
loto.zeroEnergyVerification: Turn power switch on left side to ON and verify no lights illuminate on control pendant.

ppe: NO GLOVES When Loading Spindle or Near Rotating Parts
hazards: Side-Mount Tool Changer (SMTC) loses 3" Z-clearance during tool swing
High-speed flying tool/workpiece ejection hazard (8,000 RPM inline direct-drive spindle, 600 IPM rapids)
Automatic axis motion during program execution
beforeUse: Machine Specs: 8,000 RPM inline direct-drive spindle, 600 IPM rapids.
Do NOT operate above 6,000 RPM without balanced tooling.
Verify tool length offsets (Z-heights) and workholding clearance (account for 3" Z-drop during SMTC swing).
duringUse: Keep one hand on E-Stop during first run prove-out at 5% rapid override.
Keep enclosure doors closed during all machining operations.
Monitor Distance-To-Go readout before tool approach.
afterUse: Brush chips ONLY when machine is powered down.

Inspect spindle taper condition & drawbar retention force
Refractometer coolant concentration check (Target: 8–10% Brix)
Clean telescoping way covers & Side-Mount Tool Changer (SMTC) arm
Clean electrical cabinet cooling filters

loto.normalShutdown: Depress E-Stop and Red Power Off button (Front right control panel).

energySources.isolationLocation: Main circuit breaker on rear cabinet / wall disconnect.
energySources.isolationProcedure: Switch Main circuit breaker to OFF position with individualized lock & tag; WAIT 5 MINUTES for vector drive capacitors to dissipate and verify vector drive voltage LED is completely OFF.

energySources.isolationLocation: Behind machine on wall air drop.
energySources.isolationProcedure: Turn red handle counterclockwise to OFF, bleed bottom filter valve, and verify pressure gauge reads 0 PSI.

loto.storedEnergyRelief: Mandatory 5-minute wait for vector drive capacitor discharge (verify LED off) + pneumatic line bleed to 0 PSI.
loto.zeroEnergyVerification: Press [POWER ON] on pendant and verify with non-contact AC voltage detector at input terminals + confirm air gauge reads 0 PSI.

ppe: NO GLOVES During Tool Loading or Spindle Operation
hazards: 12,000 RPM high-speed spindle and 1,400 IPM high-velocity rapids
Unbalanced toolholder ejection at >=10,000 RPM
High-pressure coolant and sharp swarf
beforeUse: Run 20-minute Spindle Warm-Up program if machine has been idle >24 hours.
Do NOT run >=10,000 RPM (requires Grade G2.5 balanced toolholders not stocked in general crib).
Clean coolant tank intake filter & chip tray screen before starting cycle.
duringUse: Perform first-run verification at 5% rapid override with hand on E-Stop and Single Block + Distance-To-Go active.
Keep enclosure doors closed and interlock engaged.
afterUse: Wash down interior ONLY with E-Stop depressed.
Shake out cloth net primary coolant tray filter into chip bin.
NEVER use compressed air inside enclosure.
sop.emergencyProtocol: Depress E-Stop immediately; report any crash, alarm code, or tool breakage to Lab Supervisor before resetting.

checklist: Refractometer coolant concentration (Target 8–10% Brix, TRIM MicroSol 585XT) & pH check
Verify Haas way lube grease/oil level & pneumatic supply pressure (85+ PSI)
Wipe 40-taper spindle & check drawbar retention force
Clean chip auger trough & coolant strainer screens
Clean vector drive cabinet air filters

assets.name: Lincoln Precision TIG 275 Welder #1
assets.conditionNote: Argon regulator leak-tested; torch cooler flow and foot pedal verified.

loto.authorizedPersonnel: Sr. Instructional Lab Supervisor (Max Wright) & Student Research Assistants (SRAs)
loto.normalShutdown: Extinguish arc, allow post-flow timer to cool tungsten, toggle main power switch OFF (Front Panel Upper Right).

energySources.isolationLocation: Wall switch box disconnect behind welder.
energySources.isolationProcedure: Pull wall switch box lever down to OFF & install LOTO lock; WAIT AT LEAST 5 MINUTES for internal capacitors to dissipate.

energySources.isolationLocation: Argon cylinder top valve & regulator assembly.
energySources.isolationProcedure: Turn cylinder top valve clockwise until all yellow (no red showing), remove gas line from regulator, depress foot pedal to purge solenoids/lines, and verify both regulator gauges read 0 PSI.

loto.storedEnergyRelief: Wait >= 5 minutes for capacitor bleed; depress foot pedal with gas disconnected to purge trapped Argon pressure.
loto.zeroEnergyVerification: Verify display is dark and cooling fan does not engage when power switch is toggled; confirm both regulator gauges read 0 PSI.

ppe: ANSI Z87.1 Safety Glasses Under Shade 10–13 Auto-Darkening Helmet
Active Fume Extraction Arm Positioned Within 12"
hazards: Intense UV/IR arc radiation (arc eye & skin burns)
High-frequency (HF) start electrical shock hazard
2,500 PSI compressed gas cylinder hazard & Argon asphyxiation in confined spaces
beforeUse: Inspect torch collet, gas lens, ceramic cup, and ground tungsten electrode.
Verify work lead (ground clamp) is securely clamped to clean bare metal.
Turn on Argon cylinder valve slowly and set flow rate (15–25 CFH).
duringUse: Keep welding curtains closed to protect bystanders from arc flash.
Observe machine duty cycle ratings and keep torch cable away from hot weldment.
afterUse: Allow post-flow Argon to cool tungsten before lifting torch.
Close Argon bottle valve completely (all yellow), purge line via foot pedal, and power machine OFF.
Coil torch and ground leads neatly on rack.
sop.emergencyProtocol: Release foot pedal immediately, switch main power OFF, close Argon cylinder valve, and alert Lab Supervisor.

checklist: Leak-test Argon regulator, flowmeter, and gas hoses with soapy water
Inspect torch collets, gas lenses, ceramic cups, and back caps for cracks/arcing
Check water cooler coolant level & return flow rate
Test foot pedal amperage potentiometer & High-Frequency (HF) start
Check work lead clamp & terminal lug tightness

assets.name: Lincoln Power MIG 255C Welder
assets.conditionNote: MIG liner blown out; contact tip and nozzle cleaned; C25 flow set to 30 CFH.

loto.authorizedPersonnel: Sr. Instructional Lab Supervisor (Max Wright) & Student Research Assistants (SRAs)
loto.normalShutdown: Extinguish arc, toggle main power switch OFF (Front Panel Bottom Left), close shielding gas cylinder valve (Rear).

energySources.isolationLocation: Wall switch box disconnect.
energySources.isolationProcedure: Pull wall switch box lever down to OFF & install LOTO lock; WAIT 5 MINUTES for internal capacitors to dissipate.

energySources.isolationLocation: Rear cylinder top valve & regulator.
energySources.isolationProcedure: Turn bottle valve clockwise until all yellow, disconnect gas line, pull MIG trigger to purge lines, and verify regulator gauges read 0 PSI.

loto.storedEnergyRelief: 5-minute capacitor bleed wait + pull MIG trigger to purge residual gas line pressure & release wire drive roll tension.
loto.zeroEnergyVerification: Verify digital wire speed/voltage displays stay dark when power switch is toggled; confirm regulator gauges read 0 PSI.

ppe: Shade 10–13 Welding Helmet + ANSI Z87.1 Safety Goggles
Flame-Resistant (FR) Clothing (No Open Pockets or Cuffs)
hazards: Hot spatter, slag burns, and UV/IR arc radiation
Powered wire feed pinch/puncture hazard at drive rolls and gun tip
Thermal overload if exceeding 40% duty cycle at 250A
beforeUse: Check wire drive roll tension and liner alignment.
Verify DC+ polarity for solid wire with gas (or DC- for flux-core).
Open C25 gas cylinder slowly and set gas flow to 25–35 CFH.
duringUse: Follow the 4-inch hand clearance rule from weld zone.
Maintain 1/4"–3/8" wire stick-out.
Respect 40% duty cycle at 250A (if thermal overload trips, let cooling fan run at idle—do not cycle power).
afterUse: Shut power switch OFF, close gas bottle valve tightly, pull trigger to purge gas line, and coil leads on hangers.
sop.emergencyProtocol: Release MIG gun trigger, turn main power switch OFF, and close gas cylinder valve.

checklist: Leak-test C25 Argon/CO2 regulator and gas hoses
Blow out MIG gun cable liner with dry compressed air
Clean anti-spatter or replace contact tip, gas diffuser, and nozzle
Inspect wire drive rolls, guide tube, and tensioner mechanism
Check ground clamp cable insulation and lug torque

energySources.isolationLocation: Wall disconnect switch behind plasma power supply.
energySources.isolationProcedure: Pull wall disconnect switch lever to OFF and install LOTO padlock & tag.

energySources.isolationLocation: Wall air supply ball valve & filter/regulator.
energySources.isolationProcedure: Close air supply ball valve, disconnect quick-connect airline, and bleed regulator to 0 PSI.

assets.name: Thermal Processing Suite: Blue M Industrial Oven & Muffle Furnace
assets.conditionNote: OTP mechanical fail-safe verified; blower bearings quiet; refractory bricks intact.

loto.authorizedPersonnel: Sr. Instructional Lab Supervisor (Max Wright) & Student Research Assistants (SRAs)
loto.normalShutdown: Blue M Oven: Lower setpoint to 167°F (75°C) and allow circulation fan to run until cooled below 167°F (turning off above 167°F seizes circulation motor bearings!), then toggle power switch OFF (Front lower center). Muffle Furnace: Press RUN key to stop heating program, toggle main power switch OFF.

energySources.isolationLocation: Wall switch box disconnect adjacent to Blue M Oven.
energySources.isolationProcedure: Pull wall switch box lever down to OFF & apply LOTO lock; verify chamber light does not illuminate.

energySources.isolationLocation: Internal stainless steel heating chamber.
energySources.isolationProcedure: Allow chamber to cool below 100°F / ambient before performing any internal maintenance.

energySources.isolationLocation: 120V power cord & wall receptacle.
energySources.isolationProcedure: Unplug power cord and secure male plug inside Rotating Electrical Plug Lockout box; verify digital display is dark.

energySources.isolationLocation: Refractory ceramic furnace chamber.
energySources.isolationProcedure: Keep door closed until internal temp is < 200°C, then crack door slightly to reach ambient room temperature before servicing.

loto.storedEnergyRelief: Blue M Oven: Mandatory fan-on cooldown < 167°F (75°C) then cool to < 100°F. Muffle Furnace: Closed-door cooldown < 200°C to prevent refractory thermal shock, then cool to ambient.
loto.zeroEnergyVerification: Verify Blue M chamber light and Muffle Furnace controller stay completely dark and chamber thermometer reads ambient (<100°F).

ppe: ANSI Z87.1 Safety Goggles / Face Shield
hazards: Extreme thermal burn and radiant heat hazard (up to 650°F in Blue M, 1,250°C in Muffle Furnace)
Explosion/fire hazard if flammable solvents, resins, or volatiles are placed inside (units are NON-explosion-proof)
Thermal burping (superheated air blast) if Blue M door is opened above 200°F
Blower motor bearing seizure if Blue M power is shut off above 167°F (75°C)
beforeUse: Strictly NO flammable solvents, uncured volatiles, or sealed containers inside either chamber.
Set Over-Temperature Protection (OTP) controller 15°C above main process setpoint.
duringUse: Follow the '200°F Rule': Do NOT open the Blue M oven door when chamber temperature exceeds 200°F to prevent thermal burping.
Use long high-temperature tongs when loading/unloading Muffle Furnace.
afterUse: Mandatory Blue M Cool-Down: Lower setpoint below 167°F (75°C) and keep blower running until chamber drops below 167°F before switching power OFF.
sop.emergencyProtocol: Shut off heating program, disconnect wall switch/plug if safe, keep chamber door CLOSED to contain any smoke/fire, and notify Lab Supervisor.

checklist: Inspect door gaskets/latches, airflow diffuser plates, and Muffle Furnace refractory bricks
Verify Over-Temperature Protection (OTP) mechanical fail-safe trip calibration
Check circulation blower motor bearing noise on Blue M industrial oven
Inspect power cords, relays, and Type-K thermocouple leads

assets.name: Vertical Metal Cutting Bandsaw
assets.conditionNote: Bi-metal blade tensioned; upper/lower blade guides adjusted.

loto.authorizedPersonnel: Sr. Instructional Lab Supervisor (Max Wright) & Student Research Assistants (SRAs)
loto.normalShutdown: Press red power switch OFF (Left side).

energySources.isolationLocation: 240V electrical plug & outlet behind saw.
energySources.isolationProcedure: Unplug power cable from outlet and install Rotating Electrical Plug Lockout (from shop fence).

loto.storedEnergyRelief: Wait for bandsaw wheels and blade to coast to a complete stop; release blade tension before changing blade.
loto.zeroEnergyVerification: Turn power switch ON and verify blade does not move.

ppe: NO GLOVES While Feeding Workpiece Near Moving Blade
hazards: Exposed vertical saw blade laceration/amputation hazard
Round stock spinning/kickback if not clamped in V-block
Gearbox tooth stripping if shifted at high RPM
beforeUse: Adjust upper blade guard to within 1/4" of top of workpiece.
Verify blade tension and proper SFPM speed for material.
NEVER shift transmission gear at high RPM (must drop RPM dial as low as possible first).
duringUse: Keep hands at least 4 inches away from blade path at all times.
Use push stick for small stock and a V-block/clamp for ALL round stock.
Make relief cuts before cutting tight radius curves.
afterUse: Wait for complete blade coast-down (never brake wheel or blade with hands).
Sweep and vacuum swarf from table and lower cabinet (no compressed air).
sop.emergencyProtocol: Hit red OFF paddle switch on left column and step back until blade stops.

checklist: Inspect blade teeth/weld integrity and verify blade tension gauge
Adjust upper/lower precision blade guides and rear thrust bearings
Clean lower wheel housing swarf and inspect rubber wheel tires

assets.name: Horizontal Wet/Dry Drop Bandsaw
assets.conditionNote: Hydraulic downfeed rate verified; auto-shutoff switch tested.

loto.authorizedPersonnel: Sr. Instructional Lab Supervisor (Max Wright) & Student Research Assistants (SRAs)
loto.normalShutdown: Turn power switch to OFF position (Front right face).

energySources.isolationLocation: Power switch & 240V wall outlet.
energySources.isolationProcedure: Turn switch down to OFF, unplug machine from outlet, and install Rotating Electrical Plug Lockout on power cable.

loto.storedEnergyRelief: Lower saw bow head fully onto horizontal rest stop and close hydraulic feed valve.
loto.zeroEnergyVerification: Turn power switch ON and verify blade does not move.

ppe: Closed-Toe Shoes (Steel-Toe Recommended for Heavy Bar Stock)
Leather Gloves ONLY While Loading Raw Bar Stock (Remove Before Running)
hazards: Blade splitting/whipping hazard on right side of machine
Crushing hazard under dropping saw head or falling cut stock
Tooth stripping on thin-wall tubing (<1/8" wall)
beforeUse: Minimum stock length is 4 inches (stock under 4" requires Shop Supervisor/SRA approval & custom fixturing).
NO thin-wall tubing under 1/8" wall thickness.
Verify coolant pump intake is submerged and adjust left blade guard close to soft jaw.
duringUse: DO NOT stand to the right side of the machine (blade splitting hazard zone).
Clamp stock securely with soft jaw and vise handwheel.
Ease saw head down gently into initial cut using hydraulic feed control.
afterUse: Wait for complete blade stop, release vise gently so heavy stock does not drop to floor, and clean chips with brush/vacuum.
sop.emergencyProtocol: Hit red E-Stop / OFF switch and close hydraulic downfeed cylinder valve immediately.

checklist: Check hydraulic downfeed cylinder feed rate & rod seals
Check flood coolant level/concentration & clean sump return screen
Inspect wire chip brush contact against blade teeth
Verify blade guide bearings & bottom auto-shutoff limit switch

assets.name: Abrasive Chop Saw
assets.conditionNote: 14" abrasive wheel inspected; lower retractable guard moves freely.

loto.authorizedPersonnel: Sr. Instructional Lab Supervisor (Max Wright) & Student Research Assistants (SRAs)
loto.normalShutdown: Release trigger (Top handle) and allow blade to come to a complete stop.

energySources.isolationLocation: 120V wall receptacle.
energySources.isolationProcedure: Unplug cord from wall and install Rotating Electrical Plug Lockout (from LoTo station by exit door).

loto.storedEnergyRelief: Wait for abrasive wheel to coast to a complete stop.
loto.zeroEnergyVerification: Depress handle trigger to verify zero electrical energy.

ppe: ANSI Z87.1 Safety Glasses + Face Shield
Heavy Leather Gloves for Raw Stock Handling Only
hazards: Abrasive wheel shattering if workpiece shifts or binds in cut
High-velocity hot spark stream fire hazard
Severe burn hazard on freshly cut steel edges
beforeUse: Verify retractable lower guard moves freely without sticking.
Inspect abrasive wheel for cracks, chips, or excessive wear.
Clamp ALL stock securely in vise (NEVER hold stock by hand).
duringUse: Keep hands >= 4 inches away from blade path.
Aim spark deflector away from trash bins and flammables.
Feed down with steady moderate pressure—do not force or twist wheel.
afterUse: Let abrasive blade coast to a complete stop before raising saw head.
Allow hot cut stock to cool or handle with pliers/leather gloves.
sop.emergencyProtocol: Release trigger immediately and keep head lowered until wheel stops spinning.

checklist: Inspect 14" abrasive wheel for cracks, glazing, and minimum wear diameter
Check pivot hinge play & head return spring tension
Inspect vise screw threads & quick-release nut engagement
Verify lower retractable safety guard operation

assets.name: 10" Bevel Compound Miter Saw
assets.conditionNote: Miter detents and retractable lower blade guard inspected and verified.

loto.authorizedPersonnel: Sr. Instructional Lab Supervisor (Max Wright) & Student Research Assistants (SRAs)
loto.normalShutdown: Release handle trigger and allow blade to coast to a complete stop.

energySources.isolationLocation: 120V wall power cord.
energySources.isolationProcedure: Unplug from wall and secure male plug inside Rotating Electrical Plug Lockout box.

loto.storedEnergyRelief: Wait for saw blade to come to a complete stop and lock head in down position if servicing.
loto.zeroEnergyVerification: Depress handle trigger to verify zero electrical energy.

hazards: Blade contact and workpiece kickback if stock is not held firmly against fence
Coast-down laceration if hands reach into kerf before blade stops
beforeUse: Verify lower retractable blade guard operates smoothly.
Lock miter and bevel angle adjustments tightly before cutting.
duringUse: Keep hands at least 6 inches away from blade path; clamp small workpieces.
Allow blade to reach full speed before feeding into stock.
afterUse: Release trigger and wait for blade to come to a complete standstill before raising head.
Vacuum sawdust and offcuts from table.
sop.emergencyProtocol: Release handle trigger immediately and keep saw head down until blade stops.

checklist: Check miter angle detents, bevel lock, & lower blade guard retraction
Inspect blade teeth for dullness or missing tips
Check arbor bolt tightness and pivot return spring

assets.name: JET Industrial Floor Drill Presses
assets.conditionNote: Quill return springs, V-belts, and drill chuck jaws inspected.

loto.authorizedPersonnel: Sr. Instructional Lab Supervisor (Max Wright) & Student Research Assistants (SRAs)
loto.normalShutdown: Toggle front main power switch OFF.

energySources.isolationLocation: 120V wall power cord.
energySources.isolationProcedure: Unplug and secure male plug inside Rotating Electrical Plug Lockout box; wait for spindle coast-down.

energySources.isolationLocation: Quill Return Spring housing (left side of head).
energySources.isolationProcedure: Retract quill fully upward to top dead center before servicing.

loto.storedEnergyRelief: Wait for complete spindle stop; retract drill press quill fully upward to relieve spring tension.
loto.zeroEnergyVerification: Toggle Drill Press power switch ON to verify zero electrical energy.

ppe: NO GLOVES on Drill Press (Rotating Spindle Entanglement Hazard)
hazards: Severe entanglement hazard if wearing gloves, long hair, or loose sleeves
Workpiece helicopter spin if not clamped to drill press table
Chuck key ejection if left in drill chuck
beforeUse: Clamp ALL workpieces securely to table or drill press vise.
Remove chuck key immediately after tightening bit.
Verify drill speed pulley setting matches drill bit diameter and material.
duringUse: Keep hands >= 4 inches from rotating chuck and drill bit.
Back out drill bit periodically to clear long stringy chips.
afterUse: Never brake rotating spindle or chuck by hand.
Brush chips from drill table and return drill bits and chuck key to rack.
sop.emergencyProtocol: Flip front paddle switch OFF immediately and step back if workpiece binds.

checklist: Inspect JET drill press spindle quill radial runout & chuck jaws
Check V-belt condition and pulley tension inside top housing
Lubricate table elevation rack/worm gear & check quill return spring tension

assets.name: General International 15-015M1 6"x48" Belt / 12" Disc Sander
assets.zone: Zone 5: Fabrication, Sheet Metal & Abrasive Finishing (FAB)
assets.conditionNote: Table-to-belt/disc gap set to 0.050" (<= 1/16"); tracking centered.

loto.authorizedPersonnel: Sr. Instructional Lab Supervisor (Max Wright) & Student Research Assistants (SRAs)
loto.normalShutdown: Red power switch to OFF position (Front face).

energySources.isolationLocation: Ceiling cord drop plug.
energySources.isolationProcedure: Unplug cord drop from ceiling receptacle and install Rotating Electrical Plug Lockout.

loto.storedEnergyRelief: Wait for abrasive belt and 12" disc to coast to a complete stop.
loto.zeroEnergyVerification: Toggle red power switch ON to verify zero electrical energy.

ppe: ANSI Z87.1 Safety Goggles + Full Face Shield
NO GLOVES STRICTLY PROHIBITED (Severe Entanglement Hazard in 1/16" Table Gap)
hazards: Fingers/gloves pulled into >1/16" gap between work table and abrasive belt/disc
Workpiece violent upward kickback if sanding on upward-travel (right) side of 12" disc
Abrasive dust inhalation and hot spark hazard
beforeUse: Verify work table-to-belt and table-to-disc gap is strictly <= 1/16" (0.0625").
Verify abrasive belt tracking and open dust collection blast gates.
duringUse: Always sand on the DOWNWARD-TRAVEL (LEFT) SIDE of the 12" disc to press stock onto table and prevent kickback.
Keep hands >= 4" away from belt/disc (use push stick for small parts and V-block for round stock).
NEVER wear gloves while operating sander.
afterUse: Wait for belt and disc to stop completely before cleaning area.
sop.emergencyProtocol: Hit red front OFF switch immediately; if stock jams in gap, do NOT attempt to free until LOTO is applied.

checklist: Check 6"x48" belt tracking & spring tensioner mechanism
Inspect graphite platen pad condition behind belt
Measure & set work table gap strictly <= 1/16" (0.0625") on both belt and 12" disc
Empty dust collection trap / spark arrestor bin

assets.name: Grizzly G0767 4"x79" Tube & Pipe Notcher
assets.zone: Zone 5: Fabrication, Sheet Metal & Abrasive Finishing (FAB)
assets.conditionNote: Grizzly G0767 4"x79" abrasive belt & mandrel roller dies inspected.

loto.authorizedPersonnel: Sr. Instructional Lab Supervisor (Max Wright) & Student Research Assistants (SRAs)
loto.normalShutdown: Push large red paddle OFF button (Left side).

energySources.isolationLocation: Ceiling drop cord.
energySources.isolationProcedure: Unplug ceiling drop cord and apply Rotating Electrical Plug Lockout; depress green start button to verify zero energy.

loto.storedEnergyRelief: Wait for 2 HP motor and 5,900 FPM abrasive belt to coast to a complete stop.
loto.zeroEnergyVerification: Depress green start button on G0767 Notcher to verify zero energy.

ppe: ANSI Z87.1 Safety Goggles + Face Shield
NO GLOVES When Operating Grizzly G0767 Tube Notcher (5,900 FPM Belt Hazard)
hazards: 2 HP motor driving abrasive belt at 5,900 FPM; severe entanglement hazard
Extreme thermal heat buildup in notched steel/chromoly tubing
beforeUse: Match grinding mandrel roller precisely to tube OD and lock quick-release vise (0–30° angle).
Inspect 4"x79" grinding belt for tears or fraying.
duringUse: Stand to the side of the Grizzly G0767 during startup.
Feed tube steadily via feed handwheel and keep hands >= 4" from moving belt.
Allow notched tubing to cool before handling.
afterUse: Power down machine, brush away grinding grit, and return mandrel rollers to rack.
sop.emergencyProtocol: Slam large red paddle OFF button on left side of G0767 Notcher.

checklist: Inspect Grizzly G0767 4"x79" belt tracking and tension
Inspect interchangeable mandrel roller bearings for play
Lubricate feed slide ways and check quick-release tube vise cam lock

assets.name: Tennsmith HBU48-16 Hand Brake & Industrial Metal Shear
assets.zone: Zone 5: Fabrication, Sheet Metal & Abrasive Finishing (FAB)
assets.conditionNote: Tennsmith HBU48-16 box fingers aligned; Shear (ID: 01166873) blade gap verified.

loto.authorizedPersonnel: Sr. Instructional Lab Supervisor (Max Wright) & Student Research Assistants (SRAs)
loto.normalShutdown: Shear (ID: 01166873): Push red power button (Right front face). Tennsmith Brake: Lower bending leaf and release clamping handle.

energySources.isolationLocation: Handle / counterweight linkage & upper clamping jaws.
energySources.isolationProcedure: Apply Chain and LOTO Lock around handle/counterweight area to prevent motion; place spacer stock beneath clamp jaws to relieve stored mechanical energy.

energySources.isolationLocation: Right-side electrical switch box.
energySources.isolationProcedure: Turn right-side electrical switch box lever to OFF and install LOTO lock; press black power button to verify zero energy.

loto.storedEnergyRelief: Place spacer stock beneath Tennsmith brake clamping jaws; wait for Shear mechanism to come to rest.
loto.zeroEnergyVerification: Press black power button on Shear to verify zero electrical energy; verify Tennsmith chain lock prevents leaf motion.

ppe: Cut-Resistant Leather Gloves for Handling Sharp Sheet Metal Edges
hazards: Tennsmith HBU48-16 Brake: 300 ft-lb counterweight swing and finger pinch hazard under box fingers
Industrial Shear: Guillotine blade amputation hazard behind hold-down guard
beforeUse: Never exceed rated mild steel capacity (16 gauge max on Tennsmith HBU48-16; never shear hardened steel, rod, or wire).
Verify all box brake fingers are tightly bolted before bending.
duringUse: Keep fingers completely clear of clamping nose bar and shear hold-down feet.
Keep bystanders clear of the 300 ft-lb counterweight arc when lifting bending leaf.
afterUse: Lower bending leaf, power down Shear, and place sheet metal offcuts in scrap bin.
sop.emergencyProtocol: Push red stop button on Shear immediately; release clamping lever on Hand Brake.

checklist: Inspect Tennsmith HBU48-16 box fingers, clamping alignment, and counterweight pivot pins
Inspect Industrial Shear (ID: 01166873) blade clearance gap and hold-down feet
Lubricate pivot joints and linkage pins

assets.name: Pedestal Bench Top Grinders & Deburring Station
assets.zone: Zone 5: Fabrication, Sheet Metal & Abrasive Finishing (FAB)
assets.conditionNote: Wheels dressed square; tool rest set to 0.050" (<= 1/16"); tongue guard <= 1/8".

loto.authorizedPersonnel: Sr. Instructional Lab Supervisor (Max Wright) & Student Research Assistants (SRAs)
loto.normalShutdown: Power switch to OFF position (Front lower center).

energySources.isolationLocation: 120V electrical cord & plug.
energySources.isolationProcedure: Unplug grinder and apply Rotating Electrical Plug Lockout to electrical plug.

loto.storedEnergyRelief: Wait for high-inertia grinding and wire wheels to coast to a complete standstill (1–2 minutes).
loto.zeroEnergyVerification: Toggle front power switch ON and verify grinding wheel does not spin.

ppe: ANSI Z87.1 Safety Glasses + Full Face Shield
NO GLOVES Near Wire or Stone Wheels (Immediate Snag Hazard)
hazards: Workpiece wedging into tool rest gap (>1/16") causing wheel explosion
High-velocity wire bristles detaching from deburring wheel
Grinding aluminum/brass on aluminum-oxide wheel (loads wheel pores and causes violent shattering)
beforeUse: Verify tool rest gap is strictly <= 1/16" (0.0625") and upper spark tongue guard is <= 1/8" (0.125").
Inspect stone wheel for cracks or non-ferrous loading.
duringUse: Stand to the side of the wheel plane during startup for 30 seconds.
Grind on the FACE of the stone wheel only (NEVER grind on the side of the wheel).
Quench hot metal frequently in water pot and hold small parts with locking pliers.
afterUse: Turn switch OFF and let wheels coast down completely.
sop.emergencyProtocol: Flip center toggle switch OFF and step out of wheel plane immediately.

checklist: Ring-test and dress grinding wheels square with diamond dresser
Adjust tool rest gap strictly <= 1/16" (0.0625") and spark arrestor tongue guard <= 1/8" (0.125")
Inspect eye shields & check wire wheel arbor nuts

assets.name: Abrasive Blast Cabinet & Hydraulic Shop Presses (Enerpac 10T & Redline 20T)
assets.zone: Zone 5: Fabrication, Sheet Metal & Abrasive Finishing (FAB)
assets.conditionNote: Blast window Mylar film replaced; Enerpac GF10P gauge & bed pins verified.

loto.authorizedPersonnel: Sr. Instructional Lab Supervisor (Max Wright) & Student Research Assistants (SRAs)
loto.normalShutdown: Blast Cabinet: Release trigger, toggle light/dust collector switch OFF (Top), close wall air drop ball valve. Hydraulic Presses: Slowly open hydraulic release valve to retract ram fully.

energySources.isolationLocation: Vacuum / cabinet light power cord.
energySources.isolationProcedure: Apply Rotating Electrical Plug Lockout over vacuum/light power cord; wait 60 seconds for dust collector impeller to stop; toggle switch ON to verify zero energy.

energySources.isolationLocation: Orange wall air valve & cabinet regulator.
energySources.isolationProcedure: Turn orange air valve OFF, disconnect airline from regulator, and depress foot pedal/trigger inside cabinet until regulator gauges read 0 PSI.

energySources.magnitude: Up to 10,000 PSI Hydraulic / 20 Tons Force
energySources.isolationLocation: Hydraulic hand/air pump release valve & H-frame bed support pins.
energySources.isolationProcedure: Open hydraulic release valve to retract cylinder ram completely (0 PSI on GF10P gauge) and verify both H-frame bed support pins are fully seated.

loto.storedEnergyRelief: Blast Cabinet: Wait 60s for impeller stop + depress foot pedal to bleed air to 0 PSI. Presses: Retract hydraulic ram until gauge reads 0 PSI.
loto.zeroEnergyVerification: Toggle cabinet switch ON (no light/vacuum), confirm air gauge reads 0 PSI, and confirm hydraulic press GF10P gauge reads 0 PSI.

ppe: Blast Cabinet: ANSI Z87.1 Safety Glasses + Integrated Cabinet Rubber Gloves
Hydraulic Presses: ANSI Z87.1 Goggles + Full Face Shield (Mandatory—Ballistic Shatter Hazard) + Steel-Toe Boots
hazards: Hydraulic Press: Ballistic part shattering under 10–20 tons of load; high-pressure hydraulic fluid injection hazard from pinhole leaks
Blast Cabinet: Dust inhalation if opened before 30s dwell time; severe slip hazard from spilled glass bead media on shop floor
beforeUse: Blast Cabinet: Inspect integrated rubber gloves for holes; turn ON dust collector before blasting; verify air regulator <= 100 PSI.

Enerpac 10T & Redline 20T Presses: Verify bed support pins are fully seated through both sides of H-frame; inspect hoses, GA2 adapter, and GF10P pressure gauge; use ONLY rated V-blocks/mandrels (NEVER use hardened chrome tool sockets).
duringUse: Blast Cabinet: Blast at 45–60° angle away from viewing window and gloves.

Hydraulic Presses: Strictly obey the 'Center Rule' (align load vertically through center of gravity); stand to the side out of the 'Line of Fire' behind Lexan/mesh shield; STOP IMMEDIATELY if gauge pressure rises without ram movement.
afterUse: Blast Cabinet: WAIT 30 SECONDS DWELL TIME after blasting before opening cabinet doors; sweep any spilled floor media immediately.
Hydraulic Presses: Slowly open release valve to retract ram; never inspect hydraulic pinhole leaks with bare hands.
sop.emergencyProtocol: Presses: Stop pumping immediately, step out of Line of Fire, and slowly crack release valve. Blast Cabinet: Release foot pedal and shut off orange air valve.

checklist: Replace blast cabinet viewing window Mylar protector film
Inspect cabinet rubber gloves, ceramic blast nozzle orifice, and dust collector filter
Inspect Enerpac RR1010 & Redline 20T hydraulic ram seals and hoses for weeping
Verify GF10P pressure gauge zero return and inspect H-frame bed pins & arbor plates for bending/deformation

assets.name: Safety Hub, LOTO Lock Center, High-Voltage Battery Bench & Paint/Prep Booth
assets.conditionNote: LOTO lock/tag inventory complete; eyewash, extinguishers & booth manometer verified.

loto.authorizedPersonnel: Sr. Instructional Lab Supervisor (Max Wright) & Student Research Assistants (SRAs)
loto.normalShutdown: Turn off Paint/Prep Booth exhaust fan switch; isolate high-voltage battery packs via manual service disconnect (MSD).

energySources.magnitude: >55–60V DC High-Voltage Tractive Packs & Li-Ion Cells
energySources.isolationLocation: Dedicated High-Voltage Battery Bench & quarantine drum.
energySources.isolationProcedure: Remove Manual Service Disconnect (MSD), apply insulated HV lockout cover, and verify 0V DC across main busbars with 1000V rated multimeter.

loto.storedEnergyRelief: Wait for HV bus discharge circuit to drop pack voltage < 5V DC; keep Class D & ABC extinguishers at arm's reach.
loto.zeroEnergyVerification: Live-Dead-Live voltage verification using rated digital multimeter.

ppe: ANSI Z87.1 Safety Glasses (Required Throughout 930 Kinnear Rd Shop)
HV Battery Bench: Class 0 High-Voltage Insulated Gloves (>55–60V), Face Shield, No Metal Jewelry
Paint/Prep Booth: Organic Vapor / Particulate Respirator & Nitrile Gloves
hazards: High-voltage DC arc flash and Li-Ion thermal runaway fire hazard
Paint/solvent vapor accumulation if booth exhaust filters are clogged
beforeUse: Verify LOTO locks, tags, hasps, and rotating plug lockouts are stocked in machine shop cage and welding room.
HV Battery Bench: Place insulating bench covers down, remove all jewelry/watches, and verify quarantine container availability per Student Motorsports Battery SOP.
duringUse: Maintain clear 36" access around all electrical panels, eyewash stations, and fire extinguishers.
Never work alone on high-voltage (>55–60V) battery systems.
afterUse: Return all LOTO devices to master board upon maintenance completion and log in shop portal.
sop.emergencyProtocol: For thermal runaway or fire: Pull fire alarm, evacuate shop, call 911 / Campus Public Safety, and notify Max Wright immediately.

checklist: Audit LOTO padlock, hasp, breaker lock, and rotating plug-lock inventory in shop cage & welding room
Verify weekly/monthly plumbed eyewash station activation & flush tags
Inspect Class ABC & Class D (combustible metal) fire extinguisher pressure gauges and inspection tags
Inspect Paint/Prep Booth differential manometer and intake/exhaust arrestor filters

assets.name: Shop Compressed Air System & Distribution Drops
assets.conditionNote: Main header holding 105 PSI; auto-drain trap and refrigerated dryer operating normally.

loto.authorizedPersonnel: Sr. Instructional Lab Supervisor (Max Wright) & Facility Maintenance
loto.normalShutdown: Place compressor controller in OFF/STOP mode and close main receiver tank outlet ball valve.

energySources.isolationLocation: Compressor room wall disconnect switch.
energySources.isolationProcedure: Pull wall disconnect lever to OFF and install LOTO padlock & tag.

energySources.magnitude: 125 PSI Receiver Tank & 80–100 PSI Distribution Header
energySources.isolationLocation: Receiver tank isolation valve & manual blowdown drain.
energySources.isolationProcedure: Close header valve, slowly open tank manual drain valve to bleed stored air pressure, and verify tank & manifold gauges read 0 PSI.

loto.storedEnergyRelief: Bleed air receiver tank and shop distribution drops completely to 0 PSI before servicing filters or regulators.
loto.zeroEnergyVerification: Verify compressor start button is dead and all pressure gauges read 0 PSI.

hazards: High-pressure hose whip if disconnected under load
Compressed air embolism hazard—NEVER direct compressed air at skin or clothing
STRICTLY NO compressed air blowdown on manual/CNC mills or lathes
beforeUse: Verify local drop regulator is set to machine specification (80–100 PSI) and inspect quick-connect coupler.
duringUse: Hold hose end firmly when disconnecting self-venting safety couplers.
afterUse: Close local drop ball valves on welding, plasma, and blast cabinet stations after use.
sop.emergencyProtocol: Close local drop ball valve or main receiver header valve and notify Lab Supervisor.

checklist: Verify automatic condensate drain trap operation on receiver tank
Check air compressor pump oil sight glass level & V-belt tension
Inspect refrigerated air dryer dew point indicator
Check wall drops & regulators (80–100 PSI) across CNC, Welding, and Fab zones for leaks or water bypass
